nodes.label: Siren Camera Infrared Flock Frame (2022-02-22 08:53:45)
nodes.description: Monochrome infrared still from the '1080P-IPC-Siren' channel at 2022-02-22 08:53:45. Despite the morning timestamp the camera is in IR night mode, so the scene is greyscale with the red feeder tops rendered as neutral grey. Small birds are scattered fairly evenly with loose aggregations in the upper right; five pan feeders hang from a horizontal pipe and a floor cable arcs across the lower third.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Siren Camera Channel
nodes.description: Camera channel labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren'. Both of its frames in this chunk are greyscale IR captures showing the same five-pan feeder line and the same floor cable arc, confirming a fixed mount and a consistent field of view across days.

nodes.label: Infrared / Low-Light Monochrome Capture Mode
nodes.description: When house lighting is dim the cameras switch to IR illumination and emit single-channel greyscale frames with flattened contrast between birds and litter. Colour cues that identify feeders and drinkers in daylight frames disappear entirely, and bird outlines merge into the substrate.
nodes.rationale: The dataset therefore contains two visually distinct domains from the same physical scene; a detector trained only on the colour frames will degrade on the IR frames, which argues for greyscale augmentation or explicit day/night domain handling rather than a single colour-dependent pipeline.
